narr: A stalled cold front residing over the Central Appalachians was the main driver behind flash flooding that occurred between August 10th and 11th. The combination of slow moving and repetitive storms led to heavy downpours through the course of the day, before finally winding down that evening as the front began moving out of the area. 24 hour rainfall amounts reported by local observers and weather stations ranged from 1.5 to 3 inches in most places, with locally higher amounts on the upwards of 5 inches observed across north-central West Virginia.||Numerous roads across the northern half of the state became flooded, primarily during the afternoon when storms were at their strongest. This resulted in a few water rescues as vehicles became submerged by the inundating rainfall. Several homes in Ritchie County became surrounded by water for a period of time as well. The most significant damage transpired in Doddridge County, where the building of the local senior center was shoved five feet off of its foundation due to the deluge of water.
ev: Sissonville High School was surrounded by high water as the nearby creek rose out of its banks. Elsewhere around Sissonville, high water was observed along several roadways, including Silent Drive, Rich Fork Road, Liverpool Lane, Sissonville Drive, Kellys Creek Road, and Legg Fork Road. Jenkins Drive also flooded north of Guthrie.||At the intersection of Martins Branch and Utah Hollow Road, a culvert collapsed due to flooding.
Near the town of Frozen, Frozen Run Road and Upper Big Run Road were impassable due to high water. A mudslide also occurred near Nicut Road.

A few homes and several roads in Smithville were flooded. Several local creeks and streams briefly rose out of their banks, which resulted in swept away cars. Debris was left behind once the water returned to its banks.
High water was observed along Spring Valley Drive. Some of the water spread into the Ceredo Volunteer Fire Station.
Flooding was observed along Route 68 south of Lubeck. This included the intersection with New England Ridge Road.

High water was observed along West Virginia Avenue east of Clarksburg. A water rescue was conducted along Wilsonburg Road. In Mount Clare, Hoop Pole Hollow Road was flooded for a brief period of time.

The Doddridge County Senior Center in West Union observed substantial damage to its foundation due to the inundation of rain. The wall inside of the building was caved in from downed trees and water rushed down the hill into the basement. Neighborhoods within West Union also suffered basement and roof damage. Minor road damage was observed within the town due to blocked culverts and small landslides.
A culvert on Trace Fork Road caved in, resulting in water surrounding a nearby home.

Water rescues occurred along Beech Hollow Road in Bridgeport and Wilsonburg Road in Clarksburg where high water was observed. Other streets flooded between Clarksburg and Bridgeport, including Boone Street, Meadland Road, Tolley Road, Tappan Road, and Sun Valley Road. 3rd Street was also impassable for a time near Nutter Fort due to high water.

High water surrounded a few homes and the post office in the town of Pullman. Local roads were also inundated with water and became impassable. A few of the local creeks and streams rose out of their banks for a brief period of time, resulting in minor flooding in locations adjacent to their banks.
Near downtown Huntington, 5th Avenue and 25th Street observed high water for a period of time.
Multiple homes were surrounded by water due to a damaged culvert in the Rosedale area.

Multiple spots of high water were observed on Fire Tower Road in the area of Craigsville, with water surrounding a nearby home. South of Craigsville, Rockcamp Run rose out of its banks and flooded Apache Road and a nearby local business. Mission Lane near Coe also observed flooding for a brief period of time.

Several houses were inundated with water in Fairplain. Charleston Road was closed for a period of time due to Grasslick Run being out of its banks in Fairplain. Portions of Charleston Road were also impassable up north in Ripley. Numerous residences were flooding in Ripley with First Avenue, Sheriff Drive, and North Church Street some of the roads impacted.
